bottom_line: Compared with placebo, apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily increased ISTH major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding (hazard ratio, 1.78; 95% confidence interval, 0.91 to 3.48; P⫽0.09).
implications: In this phase 2 trial, adding apixaban to antiplatelet therapy increased major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding versus placebo (e.g., HR 2.45 [95% CI, 1.31 to 4.61] for 10 mg once daily), while ischemic events were numerically lower but not statistically significant (e.g., HR 0.61 [95% CI, 0.35 to 1.04] for 10 mg once daily), so the results support increased bleeding risk with only suggestive evidence of reduced ischemic events within the reported confidence intervals.

major_points.text: Phase 2, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging trial in recent ACS patients on antiplatelet therapy.
major_points.quote: Apixaban for Prevention of Acute Ischemic and Safety Events (APPRAISE) was a phase 2, double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging study.

major_points.text: Patients with recent ST-elevation or non–ST-elevation ACS were randomized to placebo or one of four apixaban doses for 6 months.
major_points.quote: Patients (n⫽1715) with recent ST-elevation or non–ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome were randomized to 6 months of placebo (n⫽611) or 1 of 4 doses of apixaban

major_points.text: Primary outcome was ISTH major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding.
major_points.quote: The primary outcome was International Society of Thrombosis and Hemostasis major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding.

major_points.quote: the 2 higher-dose apixaban arms were discontinued because of excess total bleeding.

major_points.text: Apixaban 10 mg once daily significantly increased major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding versus placebo.
major_points.quote: 10 mg once daily (hazard ratio, 2.45; 95% confidence interval, 1.31 to 4.61; P⫽0.005) resulted in a dose-dependent increase in major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding.
